plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The rigid solution space corresponds to analytic functions satisfying a linear PDE (e.g., $f'(x)=0$ or $f''(x)=0$), where the solution dimension is finite and independent of sample count $w$, while the fat space corresponds to functions with infinite-dimensional solution manifolds (e.g., high-order polynomials or chaotic oscillations) that cannot be constrained by finite samples.

steps.description: Implement the `family` function that generates two function families (rigid and fat) with properly normalized outputs, ensuring Xv/X are disjoint and y/yv are (N,1) shaped arrays. The rigid family will be low-order linear PDE solutions (e.g., f''(x)=0 → linear functions) where N_c is finite and small, while the fat family will be high-order polynomials with large dynamic range that are unreachable within h≤64. Ensure y values are normalized to O(1) std before returning.
